passage:
Thursday, 10:40 pm
Almost did something dumb today.
At six a text said my bank account would be blocked tonight unless I updated my KYC through a link. The sender looked like the bank's name, but one letter was off. My thumb was right over the link.
I made myself do the boring thing: closed the message, opened the bank's own app, logged in normally. No alerts. No pending KYC.
An hour later someone called, very polite, "from the bank", saying an OTP had come to my phone and I should read it out to stop the block. I said, "Banks never ask for OTPs. I'll call the number on my card." He hung up before I finished.
I called the real number and reported both. At dinner I told Leela, and she forwarded my screenshot to her parents.
Note to self: urgency is the hook. Slow is safe.
Saurabh

qa.q: What was off about the sender's name?
qa.a: The sender looked like the bank's name, but one letter was off.

qa.q: How did Saurabh feel with a thumb right over the link?
qa.a: Saurabh felt the pull of panic about the block tonight and nearly acted before thinking.
Opening the bank's own app directly instead of the link, refusing to read out the OTP, and calling the number on the card to report both.

qa.q: How might Leela's parents benefit from the screenshot?
qa.a: They get a clear example of the fake message before it reaches them, so they are less likely to be rushed into clicking.

grounding: A person checks the sender, opens the bank's official app directly, refuses to share an OTP and reports the fake messages.

passage:
Abhinav: bro urgent. sms says electricity will be cut at 9:30 tonight, bill not updated. says call this number or click link
Uday: don't click. who's the sender?
Abhinav: some random 10 digit number
Abhinav: but it's 9:05!! work from home tomorrow, can't lose power
Uday: the power board doesn't text from personal numbers. open the official electricity app or site directly and check ur bill
Abhinav: ok checking
Abhinav: bill paid. no dues
Uday: there u go
Abhinav: i already called them tho. guy said he'd send an OTP to verify
Uday: DO NOT share it. no real company needs ur OTP. hang up if he calls again
Abhinav: he's calling again right now
Uday: decline. then report the number on the cybercrime portal. i'll send u the official link, not some random one
Abhinav: declined. heart still racing
Uday: that's how they want u to feel. slow is safe

qa.q: At what time did the SMS say the electricity would be cut?
qa.a: It said the electricity would be cut at 9:30 tonight.

qa.q: What was Abhinav feeling after declining the call?
qa.a: Abhinav's heart was still racing with the panic the scammers wanted to create.

qa.q: What did Uday tell Abhinav to do instead of clicking?
qa.a: Uday told Abhinav to check the bill on the official electricity app or site directly, never share the OTP, decline the call and report the number.

qa.q: What would change if Abhinav had read out the OTP?
qa.a: The caller could have used it to get into Abhinav's accounts, turning a fake bill scare into a real loss.

grounding: Uday talks Abhinav through a fake power-cut text, checking the official app directly and refusing to share an OTP.
